title: Makefile: build podman/quadlet before running localsystem/remotesystem
body:
**Diff:**
```diff
 .PHONY: localsystem
-localsystem: ## Run system tests locally (test/system/)
+localsystem: bin/podman bin/quadlet ## Run system tests locally (test/system/)

 .PHONY: remotesystem
-remotesystem: ## Run system tests for remote client (test/system/)
+remotesystem: podman-remote quadlet ## Run system tests for remote client (test/system/)
```

**Verification:**

Before, clean checkout, no `bin/` directory:
```
$ make -n localsystem
```
```
rm -f -rf ... (wipe)
PODMAN=.../bin/podman QUADLET=.../bin/quadlet bats ...
```
No build step.

After:
```
$ make -n localsystem
```
```
CGO_ENABLED=1 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build ... -o bin/podman ./cmd/podman
test -z "" || chcon -t container_runtime_exec_t bin/podman
CGO_ENABLED=1 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build ... -o bin/quadlet ./cmd/quadlet
rm -f -rf ... (wipe)
PODMAN=.../bin/podman QUADLET=.../bin/quadlet bats ...
```

Same before/after pattern confirmed for `remotesystem` (`bin/podman-remote` and `bin/quadlet` now build first).

I ran this dry-run comparison twice, on two separate checkouts of the same commit and got identical output both times.

**What I didn't verify:** a full real build and test run. `bin/podman` doesn't compile on this machine because `cmd/podman`'s cgo dependencies (`gpgme`, `libseccomp`) aren't installed on my system, and I don't have root on this box to install them. So I can't show the full test suite running green after the fix, only that Make's own plan now includes the missing build step, where before it didn't.

Fixes #30290

Built by claude code | reviewed & verified by me (to the best of my abilities)

comments.body: forgot to sign dco, latest commit is that

> I don't want this, I often intentionally run an old binary against new tests. So I Really do not want to rebuild each time the target is invoked.
> 
> And if we wanted this then it is not a complete thing either. Like 2e2 tests api tests,etc... all would need behave in the similar way. The way it is right now I think is best that tests do not build the main podman binaries.

ahh makes sense, thanks for the explanation as i wasn't aware that running an old binary against new tests was an intentional , and doing it for just these two targets while e2e/api tests stay as-is would be inconsistent anyway.

therefore closing this, the dependency isn't actually missing, it's deliberate. sorry for the noise. thx for the review
